I am growing cassava on this rented plot, probably with some beans or maize between the rows, because cassava can survive the long dry months we get here in Mwanza. Since the land is not mine and money is tight, I will not buy chemical fertilizer, pesticides, or hire any workers. My family will manage all the work with hand hoes, and I will add whatever cow manure we have to keep the soil from getting too weak. I will plant our own cassava cuttings saved from last season because the improved ones are hard to find in the market and cost too much.
